title: Beyond the 956: Humberto Padgett, Mexican investigative journalist and author, dies at 51
excerpt: Mexican investigative journalist and author Humberto Padgett has died at 51. His death on November 22, 2026, was confirmed by his wife and reported by RÉCORD and El Universal; he had battled tongue cancer for more than a year.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Mexican investigative journalist and author Humberto Padgett León has died at 51.

Padgett died on Sunday, November 22, 2026, at his home, surrounded by his loved ones, after more than a year battling tongue cancer. His death was confirmed by his wife, journalist Mariel Ibarra Falcón, in a post on social media, and reported by RÉCORD and El Universal.

Padgett publicly shared in August 2025 that he had advanced cancer of the mouth. He underwent chemotherapy and radiotherapy and had surgery in which part of his tongue was removed. The cancer later spread to his neck, lungs and pleura, the membrane that lines the lungs.

Born in Toluca, Estado de México, in 1975, Padgett studied journalism at the Facultad de Estudios Superiores Acatlán of the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM). Over more than two decades, he specialized in investigations into drug trafficking, organized crime, corruption, violence and human rights violations.

He worked with outlets including Reforma, emeequis and SinEmbargo, and appeared on Ciro Gómez Leyva’s programs on Radio Fórmula and Imagen Televisión. One of his best-known investigations, in 2017, exposed drug sales at Ciudad Universitaria, the UNAM campus; he was attacked and threatened during that work.

As an author, he wrote books on violence and social reality in Mexico, including Las muertas del Estado, Jauría: la verdadera historia del secuestro en México, Historias mexicanas de mujeres asesinas, Los muchachos perdidos, and Guerrero: los hombres de verde y la dama de rojo.

His journalism earned national and international recognition, including the Premio Nacional de Periodismo in 2007 and the Premio Internacional de Periodismo Rey de España in 2010.

Rest in Peace, Humberto Padgett.

Sources: RÉCORD; El Universal.
